event.summary: Legacy tmux scrollback is intentionally discarded on update
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

TLDR: Updating ends old terminals and their scrollback; restarting an old session begins with an empty terminal.

Details: Assigned patch lines 303–488 remove capture_pane_history, which previously copied tmux history on Restart. Could-be-highest: yes, if destroying retained terminal output were an unintended loss of user-owned work. Suggested bucket: highest consequence considered, proposed drop for explicit specification acceptance. Confidence: confirmed specification acceptance; source-only review, no execution. SPEC.md at this revision, Terminal experience, lines 3004–3016, explicitly says: 'This release ends them: the first time a host’s supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server' (apostrophe normalized here), and 'After an update to this release, Restart, Clone and Replace start such a session in a new, empty terminal.' SPEC_impl.md, Terminal substrate: private tmux server, lines 2882–2889, states that the running supervisor runs no tmux and its driver is gone. The proposed consequence is the requested retirement, rather than evidence of an accidental regression. proposed_drop: explicit product acceptance, exact decisive text: 'After an update to this release, Restart, Clone and Replace start such a session in a new, empty terminal.' possible_cover: none; no coverage sources read. Caveat: replacement host-to-host Restart still owes its separate scrollback contract; that interface remains to be checked.

event.summary: Retiring legacy tmux terminals destroys their retained output
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

TLDR: Updating ends old tmux terminals, their processes and retained screen/scrollback. Restart of such a session begins with an empty terminal.

Details: Revision of c1 from candidate to finding as required for specification-accepted potentially-highest consequences. Original consequence preserved: removal of capture_pane_history eliminates the old tmux-to-host Restart history-copy path and the retirement destroys old retained terminal output. Suggested bucket: highest, loss of potentially user-owned terminal output/processes; could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: confirmed by source and explicit contract, not execution. proposed_drop: proposed only, not accepted by parent; SPEC.md:3004–3016 explicitly authorizes ending old tmux terminals and says exactly, 'After an update to this release, Restart, Clone and Replace start such a session in a new, empty terminal.' It separately says, 'A session whose agent or tabs already run in terminal hosts keeps them.' SPEC_impl.md:2880–2926 specifies startup retirement and legacy-row conversion. The accepted boundary covers the designated old tmux server and its attributed legacy work only; it does not authorize wrong-target kills, loss of host-terminal output, or stopping surviving host tabs. Prior source checks: core.rs:6142–6183 performs retirement before reload; core.rs:6675–6679 never reconstructs legacy panes; core.rs:13000–13028 calls host relaunch; host_restart.rs:418–457 retains host history seeding and :237–255 passes the seed to the replacement. These checks supported the narrow retirement acceptance but did not alone prove the complete replacement lifecycle or absence of wrong-target actions. Those interfaces are being rechecked in this synthesis turn. possible_cover: none. Caveats: no execution or reproduction; independent drop check remains required. Prior records remain append-only, and no parent drop approval is inferred.

event.summary: Retiring legacy tmux terminals destroys their retained output
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

TLDR: Updating ends old tmux terminals, their processes and retained screen/scrollback. Restart of such a session starts with an empty terminal. The assigned removal does not itself establish loss of a surviving terminal host's history or processes.

Details: Original consequence retained: removing capture_pane_history removes tmux-to-host history transfer, while startup retirement destroys the legacy server's retained output and ends old work. Revised attribution: git diff --numstat of service/core/old_terminals.rs between this commit and its parent is empty; the parent already invokes OldTerminals::end_private_server at core.rs:6433–6438, calls tmux.no_server_after_startup, and returns None for legacy row lookup at :6965–6969. Therefore the deletion removes a path already unreachable through normal reload, rather than independently introducing the retirement. Suggested bucket: highest consequence considered, loss of potentially user-owned output/processes; could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: source-confirmed retirement consequence and narrow contract acceptance; no execution. proposed_drop: proposed only, parent has accepted no drop. Exact acceptance at SPEC.md:3006–3010: 'This release ends them: the first time a host's supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program.' SPEC.md:3016 says, 'After an update to this release, Restart, Clone and Replace start such a session in a new, empty terminal.' Exact exclusion at :3013: 'A session whose agent or tabs already run in terminal hosts keeps them.' SPEC.md:1938–1952 separately requires retained host scrollback, a blank new screen, rollback of a confirmed-ended failed replacement, and keeping tabs running.

Replacement lifecycle checks/results: core.rs:12381–12483 pins the old child and sweeps AgentOnly; :12486–12493 reads the old host seed before opening a generation. host_restart.rs:418–490 waits for settled final output, asks history_seed(MAX_SNAPSHOT), preserves old size, logs missing history and refuses cancellation during supervisor stop. Its :237–255 passes the blob to the spawned replacement; :294–388 publishes before ending only the captured replacing host. :740–782 confirms failed replacement cleanup and sweeps AgentOnly before definitive rollback. core.rs:12798–12975 skips restoration after publication, restores prior terminal only on definitive failure, leaves ambiguous replacement terminal-less, and retains shared tab cells. host_handover.rs:645–861 filters agent rows by Host kind, adopts by session and generation, and excludes Tab roles from earlier-agent cleanup. :875–980 checks session/agent/generation for earlier-host fallback and refuses an unreadable newer record; :992–1053 supersedes only an earlier Agent host of a confirmed later Host row naming another socket, never a current host or tab. These are source refutations of specific highest routes: confusing surviving tabs with the retired agent, deleting a current host as superseded, choosing older readable history over an unreadable newer record, or rolling back a successfully published replacement to its old terminal.

Startup retirement boundary: old_terminals.rs:290–349 sweeps converted legacy agents with AgentOnly and old tabs by Tab id, never WholeSession. :363–408 excludes recorded host tabs from scope-derived old tabs. The private-server shutdown is pinned to its peer/start identity and socket command line (previously checked :176–279); the retirement allowance does not authorize a wrong-target action. No such route from the assigned removal was established. Source-refuted wrong-target close routes remain separately recorded in c2. Exact accepted host residuals are separate from tmux retirement: SPEC.md:1942–1945 allows terminal-less ambiguous failed replacement and starts empty when old history cannot be copied; SPEC_impl.md:2417–2419 says an ambiguously failed restart can leave the old host/history alive while the next Restart starts empty. These residuals are preserved as caveats, not generalized permission to discard surviving host work. possible_cover: none. Independent checking of all proposed drops remains required; no runtime behavior was observed and no reproduction was written.

event.summary: Removing tmux pane identity checks does not remove tab-close identity checks
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

TLDR: Considered whether stale tab cleanup could stop another tab or an agent after the tmux identity guard was removed. The replacement retains an identity guard.

Details: Assigned patch lines 1–52 remove kill_window, including its same-command pane/session identity check against tmux target fallback. Could-be-highest: yes; stopping another live terminal would lose user-owned processes. Suggested bucket: highest consequence considered, proposed drop because the suspected route is refuted by the replacement. Confidence: confirmed source refutation, no execution. At the reviewed commit, service/core.rs:6675–6679 never reconstructs a tmux terminal from a legacy row. service/core/host_tabs.rs:915–927 re-resolves the tab in this session’s tab cell, filters by equality with the captured HostTerminal, and rejects the session’s agent runtime. Lines 964–969 recheck automatic-close eligibility under the lifecycle claim, and lines 1052–1062 end the adopted process or selected host rather than a tmux current-window fallback. SPEC_impl.md, Tabs in hosts, states: 'the session’s cell holds only hosts whose tag names one of its tabs (the open wrote it, a reload checked it), and the agent’s own runtime is refused' (typographic apostrophes normalized in this quotation). proposed_drop: replacement host identity and lifecycle checks refute the stale tmux-target route; exact code predicates are find_host_tab(...).filter(|tab| tab.host == host) and Some(agent) if *agent == tab.host. possible_cover: none. Caveat: this is a check of deletion’s implications, not a comprehensive independent review of host process identity mechanisms.

event.summary: Stale tab cleanup route is refuted by replacement lifecycle identity checks
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

TLDR: Original suspected consequence preserved: deleting tmux's guarded kill could let stale tab cleanup stop another tab or an agent and lose its processes. The replacement's normal shipped close path does not use tmux target fallback and retains separate terminal identity checks.

Details: Could-be-highest: yes, wrong-terminal termination would lose user-owned processes. Suggested bucket: highest consequence considered; confidence: source-refuted for the identified stale/fallback routes, no execution. proposed_drop: proposed source refutation only; parent has accepted no drop. Checks/results: core.rs:14005–14058 moves the session lifecycle claim onto the supervisor-owned close task, resolves TerminalId::Tab(tab_id), and dispatches only that runtime. terminals.rs:225–248 resolves from the session's tab cell and returns NotFound without agent fallback. host_tabs.rs:915–927 requires the same tab id and HostTerminal as resolved, refuses the agent runtime; hosts/terminal.rs:1467–1469 defines equality by Arc::ptr_eq. host_tabs.rs:964–969 rechecks automatic-reap eligibility before mutation, :982–1012 roots the initial sweep only at the pinned live child and uses marker-only cleanup after host shutdown; core.rs:14120–14178 derives this tab's scope and SweepTarget::Tab(tab_id), with failed cleanup refused. host_tabs.rs:1052–1062 checks the adopted process when the socket alone was judged gone. host_launch.rs:682–719 first shuts down the held runtime, then aborts it and signals its pinned adopted process; :727–745 uses terminate_verified, without reconnecting to a replacement socket when an adopted process exists. Its no-adopted-process fallback (:753–800) shuts down a readable host only when its tag names this session; unreadable connections need a peer to signal. Socket cleanup (:812–814) takes host_scan and uses re-verifying removal. Exact contract, SPEC_impl.md:2332–2338: 'Closing a tab: the session's cell holds only hosts whose tag names one of its tabs (the open wrote it, a reload checked it), and the agent's own runtime is refused'; also 'the sweep roots at the child only while it runs'. This refutes (1) tmux falling back from a vanished pane to a current window, (2) re-resolving a different runtime after asynchronous work, (3) recycled child pid becoming a sweep root, and (4) reconnecting to and killing a new socket occupant when an adopted process exists. No highest route is dropped on retirement acceptance: these are separate source checks. possible_cover: none. Caveats: the no-adopted-process fallback validates session identity rather than role/generation; no shipped collision/replacement route from this deletion has been established, and this record does not claim that arbitrary corrupted state or an externally replaced socket is fully protected. Broader process-sweep correctness is outside this assigned deletion. Independent check remains pending.

These are separate source checks, not consequences waived by tmux retirement. possible_cover: none. event.summary: Removing tmux resize clamping does not newly break host resize handling
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether deleting the tmux resize helper's dimension clamping newly lets an invalid viewer size fail the connection or other sessions. The surviving host path still logs the refusal locally and already used the same size validation before the entire reviewed range. Suggested bucket: other if established; could-be-highest: no security or user-work-loss route. Confidence: source refutation of this removal consequence; no execution. proposed_drop: exact source equivalence and failure handling, not a policy waiver. Assigned patch lines 151–180 delete resize_window, which clamped tmux dimensions and bounded its exchange. Current handlers.rs:2028–2074 checks the route session and attachment channel/connection under the attachments lock, then :2075–2083 invokes the selected HostTerminal resize and only warns on error. hosts/terminal.rs:2344–2353 rejects invalid size synchronously and coalesces valid requests through a watch channel, so the removed tmux subprocess wait is not inherited by another global-lock operation. At exclusive base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a, service/terminals.rs:271–284 already dispatches Terminal::Host directly to host.resize(Size { cols, rows }); only Terminal::Tmux uses the deleted clamping helper. The immediate parent handlers.rs:2438–2452 likewise only logs resize failure. Therefore no invalid-size connection failure or host-clamping regression from these assigned lines is established. possible_cover: none in supplied neighbour records; this is a non-reporting decision, not a novel defect. Caveat: invalid host sizes are refused, rather than clamped; this comparison does not claim that every viewport geometry is accepted or validate unrelated browser sizing behavior.
